meta.title: Click- and motion-latency tables with test conditions
chart_suggestions: Bar (sorted): piaknow motion latency at 8 kHz, wired solid / wireless hatched; XA25 and V4 Pro highlighted
XY: report rate (log x) vs motion latency for V4 Pro wired, V4 Pro wireless, OP1 8k V2, GPX2 wireless, with the T/2 floor line; region under the best curve shaded as the sweet spot
Grouped bar with 95% CI: XBAB XA25 vs OP1 8k v2, 4 panels
Bar: click latency by method family (electrical, end-to-end finger model) - never mix methods on one axis
warnings: Do not compare numbers across methods: TPU electrical click latency (us), XBAB electrical (us), Finalmouse end-to-end with finger travel (ms) and RTINGS (paywalled) measure different things.
piaknow rows marked * ran with Motion Sync forced on (may be inaccurate). Smoothing filters inflate motion latency in this method.

source.source_title: piaknow, "Motion Latency of Some Computer Mice 2026-09-15" (chart image attached to the X post of 2026-09-15; read from the original 3629 x 2664 image)
source.label: IM
source.note: Post text: "Since the data is getting old, I have decided to publish all of my mouse motion latency test results that I have been collecting for the past 2 years. ... My paper about the methods is nearly finished." Attached video shows the measurement setup.

motion_latency_piaknow_2026_09_15.method: Every measurement at 1600 cpi, performance options (e.g. sensor frame rate) at maximum, other options default. Motion latency D(t_in) = lim(dt->0+) t_out(t_in, dt) - t_in, averaged over time; does not model smoothing, so mice with smoothing filters are often overestimated (by roughly 1-2x the (n-1)dt/2 SMA delay).

footnotes.*: Measured with "Motion Sync" forcibly enabled at 4000 Hz report rate or below; behaviour not modelled, results may be inaccurate.
footnotes.**: SPI reading not synchronized with USB polling, but an intentional frequency offset means no long-term drift in motion latency.
footnotes.***: SPI reading synchronized with USB polling only at 1000 Hz or below.
footnotes.****: 1000 Hz measured over Full-Speed USB; 2000/4000 Hz omitted (report interval not an integer multiple of its minimum, incompatible with the data-correction method).

source.note: Manufacturer-run comparison (XBAB measured its own mouse vs a competitor) with full method disclosed; labelled MC, not IM.

click_latency_xbab_vs_op1_8k_v2.post_text: XA25 (NC Release) / OP1 (GX Speed): XA25 wins by 248 us. XA25 (SR Latch) / OP1 (GX Safe): XA25 wins by 1 us. Measured by our Beagle USB 480 Protocol Analyzer. Then we tested again with sensor motion involved.

definitions.NC Release / GX Speed: NC edge -> USB data (switch reported when the normally-closed contact opens)
definitions.SR Latch / GX Safe: NO edge -> USB data (set-reset latch on the normally-open contact)
definitions.note: NC edge precedes NO edge by ~1.5 ms due to switch motion. Values are electrical latency, measured by Beagle USB 480.

derived.unit: us added when the sensor is moving (moving - stationary)
derived.label: DV
derived.note: OP1 8k v2 adds ~121-125 us to a click while the sensor is moving; XA25 adds none within CI. Design target for Theseus: "a click never waits for motion" (same principle stated in the Kunai guide).

derived.unit: us net head start of NC-release (GX Speed) over NO-latch (GX Safe) on the OP1, stationary
derived.label: DV
derived.formula: ~1500 us NC-before-NO switch motion - (320.29 - 65.63) us extra electrical latency = ~1245 us
derived.note: consistent with TechPowerUp's "GX Speed about 1.4 ms faster" (deck source tpuOp1); ~1.5 ms is XBAB's approximate figure
